quests.explanation: 'People who' takes a plural verb, and 'the hardest part is…' is a natural way to name the main difficulty.
quests.textToSpeak: People who commute long distances every day often say the hardest part is the unpredictability.
quests.correctAnswer: People who commute long distances every day often say the hardest part is the unpredictability.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Commute' /kəˈmjuːt/ is stressed on MUTE. 'Unpredictability' /ˌʌnprɪˌdɪktəˈbɪləti/ has seven syllables with main stress on BIL.

quests.hint: 'The customers we spoke to' has no relative word.
quests.explanation: English drops 'that' or 'who' when the noun is the object, and 'to' stays at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: Most of the customers we spoke to said they'd happily pay more for faster delivery.
quests.correctAnswer: Most of the customers we spoke to said they'd happily pay more for faster delivery.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Happily' /ˈhæpɪli/. 'Delivery' /dɪˈlɪvəri/ is stressed on LIV. 'They'd' /ðeɪd/ means 'they would'. 'Most of the' links quickly.

quests.hint: Break the sentence at 'who was standing near the exit'.
quests.explanation: The 'who' clause identifies the person, and the past perfect 'had been closed' shows an earlier event.
quests.textToSpeak: Somebody who was standing near the exit told me the front entrance had been closed.
quests.correctAnswer: Somebody who was standing near the exit told me the front entrance had been closed.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Exit' /ˈeksɪt/ or /ˈeɡzɪt/. 'Entrance' /ˈentrəns/ is stressed on EN. 'Somebody' /ˈsʌmbədi/. 'Closed' ends in /zd/.

quests.hint: Say 'work out why' as a unit.
quests.explanation: After 'why', the clause keeps statement order, and 'kept + -ing' describes a repeated fault.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody could work out why the system kept logging people out every few minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Nobody could work out why the system kept logging people out every few minutes.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Logging' /ˈlɒɡɪŋ/. 'System' /ˈsɪstəm/ is stressed on SIS. 'People' /ˈpiːpl/. 'Every few' links: ev-ry-few.

quests.hint: After 'remind me where', use 'we agreed', not 'did we agree'.
quests.explanation: Embedded questions keep statement order, which is what makes this sentence sound natural.
quests.textToSpeak: Can you remind me where we agreed to meet before the presentation starts?
quests.correctAnswer: Can you remind me where we agreed to meet before the presentation starts?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Remind' /rɪˈmaɪnd/. 'Agreed' /əˈɡriːd/ ends in /d/. 'Presentation' is stressed on TAY. 'Before the' links. Your voice rises on the request.

quests.explanation: 'I have no idea how…' expresses genuine surprise, and 'managed to' shows the achievement.
quests.textToSpeak: I honestly have no idea how they managed to finish the whole project in three weeks.
quests.correctAnswer: I honestly have no idea how they managed to finish the whole project in three weeks.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Honestly' /ˈɒnɪstli/. 'Whole' /həʊl/ starts with /h/. 'Project' /ˈprɒdʒekt/ is stressed on PROJ. 'Three' starts with /θ/.

quests.hint: 'Hesitate' is stressed on the first syllable.
quests.explanation: This is a standard polite closing in emails and letters.
quests.textToSpeak: If you need any further help, please don't hesitate to contact us.
quests.correctAnswer: If you need any further help, please don't hesitate to contact us.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Hesitate' /ˈhezɪteɪt/. 'Further' /ˈfɜːðə/. 'Contact' /ˈkɒntækt/. 'Don't hesitate' has a light /t/ before /h/.

quests.explanation: 'Supposing' opens a hypothetical, and the next clause asks about a practical solution.
quests.textToSpeak: Supposing the flight is delayed, do we have a backup plan for getting to the hotel?
quests.correctAnswer: Supposing the flight is delayed, do we have a backup plan for getting to the hotel?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Supposing' /səˈpəʊzɪŋ/ is stressed on POH. 'Backup' /ˈbækʌp/ is stressed on BACK. 'Getting to' links smoothly.

quests.explanation: 'Provided that' sets a condition that must be met, and it's common in workplace planning.
quests.textToSpeak: Provided that everyone sends me their feedback by Wednesday, we can finalize the report by Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: Provided that everyone sends me their feedback by Wednesday, we can finalize the report by Friday.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Provided' /prəˈvaɪdɪd/ is stressed on VIDE. 'Finalize' /ˈfaɪnəlaɪz/. 'Wednesday' /ˈwenzdeɪ/ has a silent 'd'.

quests.hint: Two past perfects: 'she'd been offered', 'she hadn't decided'.
quests.explanation: The past perfect shows that these events came before the moment she was speaking.
quests.textToSpeak: She mentioned that she'd been offered another job, but she hadn't decided whether to accept it.
quests.correctAnswer: She mentioned that she'd been offered another job, but she hadn't decided whether to accept it.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Mentioned' /ˈmenʃnd/. 'Accept' /əkˈsept/ is stressed on SEPT. 'She'd' /ʃiːd/. 'Whether to' links.

quests.explanation: 'According to' reports someone else's information, and 'although' adds a complaint.
quests.textToSpeak: According to Ben, the client expects a full report by Monday, although nobody told us.
quests.correctAnswer: According to Ben, the client expects a full report by Monday, although nobody told us.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'According' /əˈkɔːdɪŋ/ is stressed on COR. 'Client' /ˈklaɪənt/. 'Expects' /ɪkˈspekts/ ends in /kts/. 'Nobody' /ˈnəʊbədi/.

quests.explanation: 'Reckon' introduces an informal opinion, and 'we'd save… if we cooked…' is the second conditional.
quests.textToSpeak: My brother reckons that we'd save a lot more money if we cooked at home more often.
quests.correctAnswer: My brother reckons that we'd save a lot more money if we cooked at home more often.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Reckons' /ˈrekənz/. 'Cooked' /kʊkt/ ends in /kt/. 'A lot more' links: ə-lot-more. 'We'd' /wiːd/.

quests.explanation: 'Whatever you decide' is a supportive opener, and 'talk it over' means discuss.
quests.textToSpeak: Whatever you decide, make sure you talk it over with your family first.
quests.correctAnswer: Whatever you decide, make sure you talk it over with your family first.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Whatever' /wɒtˈevə/. 'Talk it over' links: tor-ki-tover. 'Family' /ˈfæməli/ is often said in three syllables.

quests.explanation: 'It might be worth + -ing' is a gentle suggestion, and 'since' gives the reason.
quests.textToSpeak: It might be worth asking around before you hire anyone, since recommendations are often more reliable.
quests.correctAnswer: It might be worth asking around before you hire anyone, since recommendations are often more reliable.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Recommendations' /ˌrekəmenˈdeɪʃnz/ is stressed on DAY. 'Reliable' /rɪˈlaɪəbl/ is stressed on LY. 'Asking around' links.

quests.hint: 'Putting it off' and 'get it over with' are both idioms.
quests.explanation: 'Put off' means delay, and 'get it over with' means finish something unpleasant quickly.
quests.textToSpeak: Instead of putting it off any longer, why not just call them and get it over with?
quests.correctAnswer: Instead of putting it off any longer, why not just call them and get it over with?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Instead of' links: in-sted-əv. 'Putting it' can sound like 'pudding-it'. 'Over with' links.

quests.hint: 'I don't mean to be rude' is a softener.
quests.explanation: This phrase prepares the listener for a request that could sound harsh.
quests.textToSpeak: I don't mean to be rude, but would you mind keeping your voice down a little?
quests.correctAnswer: I don't mean to be rude, but would you mind keeping your voice down a little?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Rude' /ruːd/ has a long vowel. 'Voice' /vɔɪs/ ends in /s/. 'Keeping' /ˈkiːpɪŋ/. 'Would you' sounds like 'woodja'.

quests.explanation: 'I couldn't help + -ing' means you noticed without trying, which makes a comment feel less like gossip.
quests.textToSpeak: It's probably nothing, but I couldn't help noticing that she seemed a bit quiet today.
quests.correctAnswer: It's probably nothing, but I couldn't help noticing that she seemed a bit quiet today.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Noticing' /ˈnəʊtɪsɪŋ/. 'Quiet' /ˈkwaɪət/. 'Couldn't' has a silent 'l'. 'Probably' is often three syllables.

quests.hint: Break after 'wrong way' and start the second chunk fresh.
quests.explanation: 'Don't take this the wrong way' prepares the listener for possible criticism.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't take this the wrong way, but I think you might have misunderstood what he meant.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't take this the wrong way, but I think you might have misunderstood what he meant.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Misunderstood' /ˌmɪsʌndəˈstʊd/ is stressed on STOOD. 'Might have' /ˈmaɪtəv/. 'Meant' /ment/ ends in /nt/.

quests.explanation: 'Might as well' means there's no reason not to, and 'since' gives the reason.
quests.textToSpeak: Since our train doesn't leave until eleven, we might as well have a proper breakfast.
quests.correctAnswer: Since our train doesn't leave until eleven, we might as well have a proper breakfast.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Proper' /ˈprɒpə/. 'Breakfast' /ˈbrekfəst/. 'Until' /ənˈtɪl/. 'Eleven' /ɪˈlevn/ is stressed on LEV.

quests.explanation: 'Whichever' means it doesn't matter which one, and 'allow at least' adds a safety margin.
quests.textToSpeak: Whichever route you take, allow at least an hour for the journey because the roads get very busy.
quests.correctAnswer: Whichever route you take, allow at least an hour for the journey because the roads get very busy.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Whichever' /wɪtʃˈevə/. 'Allow' /əˈlaʊ/. 'Journey' /ˈdʒɜːni/ starts with /dʒ/. 'At least' links: a-tleast.

quests.hint: 'Turned out to be' is a fixed chunk.
quests.explanation: 'Turned out to be' describes a surprising discovery, and 'packed with' means full of.
quests.textToSpeak: The guidebook made it sound quiet, but the place turned out to be packed with tourists.
quests.correctAnswer: The guidebook made it sound quiet, but the place turned out to be packed with tourists.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Guidebook' /ˈɡaɪdbʊk/. 'Tourists' /ˈtʊərɪsts/ ends in /sts/. 'Packed' /pækt/. 'Sound quiet' links.

quests.explanation: The past perfect 'I'd never tried' sets up earlier experience, and 'spent… falling' describes how time went.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd never tried surfing before, so I spent most of the lesson falling off the board.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd never tried surfing before, so I spent most of the lesson falling off the board.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Surfing' /ˈsɜːfɪŋ/. 'Lesson' /ˈlesn/. 'Falling off' links: fall-ing-off. 'Board' /bɔːd/.

quests.explanation: 'The moment' starts a sequence, and 'smell something burning' uses -ing after a sense verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The moment I opened the door, I could smell something burning, and I ran straight to the kitchen.
quests.correctAnswer: The moment I opened the door, I could smell something burning, and I ran straight to the kitchen.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Burning' /ˈbɜːnɪŋ/. 'Straight' /streɪt/. 'Kitchen' /ˈkɪtʃɪn/. 'Opened' /ˈəʊpənd/.

quests.explanation: 'Had only been… when…' marks how soon something became clear, and the second past perfect shows nobody had prepared.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd only been there for ten minutes when it became obvious that nobody had prepared anything.
quests.correctAnswer: We'd only been there for ten minutes when it became obvious that nobody had prepared anything.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Obvious' /ˈɒbviəs/. 'Prepared' /prɪˈpeəd/. 'Became' /bɪˈkeɪm/. 'Nobody' /ˈnəʊbədi/.

quests.explanation: 'Personally, I think' clearly marks an opinion, and 'how much time' turns the point into a noun clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Personally, I think social media's biggest problem is how much time it takes from real conversations.
quests.correctAnswer: Personally, I think social media's biggest problem is how much time it takes from real conversations.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Personally' /ˈpɜːsənəli/ is stressed on PER. 'Conversations' /ˌkɒnvəˈseɪʃnz/. 'Media's' /ˈmiːdiəz/. 'Takes from' links.

quests.explanation: 'Switch off' means stop thinking about work, and 'harder to' balances the opening claim.
quests.textToSpeak: There's no doubt that technology has made life easier, but it's also made it harder to switch off.
quests.correctAnswer: There's no doubt that technology has made life easier, but it's also made it harder to switch off.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Doubt' /daʊt/. 'Technology' /tekˈnɒlədʒi/ is stressed on NOL. 'Easier' /ˈiːziə/. 'Switch' ends in /tʃ/.

quests.hint: 'You could argue that' introduces an opinion.
quests.explanation: 'You could argue' presents a view without fully committing, and 'it depends on' adds nuance.
quests.textToSpeak: You could argue that shopping online is more convenient, although it depends on what you're buying.
quests.correctAnswer: You could argue that shopping online is more convenient, although it depends on what you're buying.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Convenient' /kənˈviːniənt/. 'Depends' /dɪˈpendz/ ends in /ndz/. 'Online' /ɒnˈlaɪn/ is stressed on LINE. 'Buying' /ˈbaɪɪŋ/.

quests.hint: 'We'd known' and 'could have' are both quick.
quests.explanation: The third conditional talks about a past situation that didn't happen and what would have followed.
quests.textToSpeak: If we'd known the roads would be this quiet, we could have left an hour later.
quests.correctAnswer: If we'd known the roads would be this quiet, we could have left an hour later.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'We'd known' /wiːd nəʊn/. 'Could have' /ˈkʊdəv/. 'Hour' /ˈaʊə/ has a silent 'h'. 'Quiet' /ˈkwaɪət/.

quests.hint: Say 'I'd been hoping to' as one quick chunk.
quests.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows a hope that lasted up to a moment in the past.
quests.textToSpeak: The person I'd been hoping to speak to is away until next week, so I left a voicemail.
quests.correctAnswer: The person I'd been hoping to speak to is away until next week, so I left a voicemail.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Voicemail' /ˈvɔɪsmeɪl/ is stressed on VOICE. 'Hoping' /ˈhəʊpɪŋ/. 'Until' /ənˈtɪl/. 'Away' /əˈweɪ/.

quests.explanation: 'Whoever' refers to an unknown person, and 'try + -ing' means test something out.
quests.textToSpeak: Whoever designed this website clearly never tried using it on a phone, because half the buttons don't work.
quests.correctAnswer: Whoever designed this website clearly never tried using it on a phone, because half the buttons don't work.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Whoever' /huːˈevə/. 'Buttons' /ˈbʌtnz/ has no clear vowel before the /n/. 'Website' /ˈwebsaɪt/. 'Clearly' /ˈklɪəli/.
